findings.title: Promised reparse-point (junction/symlink) check is not implemented; links can escape the allowed folder.
findings.body:
The PR's security model says each component of the resolved path is rejected if it has `FileAttributes.ReparsePoint`, because checking the path text alone does not stop redirection. Neither `TryResolveVirtualUrl` nor the serving code in `MarkdownPreviewHandlerControl` checks attributes. The only check is `GetFullPath` plus `GetRelativePath`.

Trigger: a document folder (for example a cloned repo or a share) contains a symlink or junction `img -> C:\Users\me` and the Markdown file has `![](img/secret.png)`. The text check passes, `File.Exists` and `File.ReadAllBytes` follow the link, and a file outside the allowed tree is served.

Fix: walk each component from `basePath` to `fullPath` and reject any that has `FileAttributes.ReparsePoint`, or compare the final target (`FileInfo.ResolveLinkTarget(true)`) against the base. Otherwise, take the claim out of the description.

findings.title: Raw-HTML hardening described in the PR (OFF-state rewrite, srcset removal) is not implemented.
findings.body: The description says that with the setting OFF, raw HTML `src` is rewritten to `#` so `data:` images cannot render. It also says `srcset` is removed from raw `` in both states. The code rewrites only when `allowLocalImages` is true and never touches `srcset`. The regex also matches only double-quoted `src`. So with the setting ON, `` is not caught: `data:` is resolved without going through the resource filter, so it renders, and no info bar is raised. Fix: either implement what the description promises (run the rewrite in both states, strip `srcset`, handle single-quoted and unquoted attributes), or correct the security model in the description.

findings.title: Virtual URL is built without escaping, so an image file name containing '#' never loads.
findings.body:
`relativePath` is added to `https://localmdimages/` as-is. For `![](images/c#-diagram.png)` the browser treats `#-diagram.png` as a fragment, so the request is for `images/c`, which returns 404 and the image does not show.

The serving side also unescapes the path, so a file literally named `a%20b.png` is looked up as `a b.png`.

Fix: build the URL from `Uri.EscapeDataString` of each path segment, so the result round-trips through `Uri.UnescapeDataString` in `TryResolveVirtualUrl`.

findings.title: Image bytes are read synchronously and without limits on the WebResourceRequested (UI) thread.
findings.body:
The handler calls `File.Exists` and `File.ReadAllBytes` on whatever file under the base path is requested. There is no size cap, no check that it is an image type, and no deferral.

Trigger: a Markdown file on a slow or unreachable UNC share, or one that references a large file (an ISO or video in the repo, or anywhere under the share root). The Explorer preview host's UI thread then blocks, or the whole file (up to about 2 GB) is loaded into memory.

Fix: use `e.GetDeferral()` and read on a background thread. Return a `FileStream` instead of reading the whole file into memory. Allow only known image extensions and set a size cap.

held.title: Only FileNotFoundException is caught when reading settings; other read errors break the whole preview.
held.body:
`GetLocalImagesEnabled` runs inside `DoPreview`'s main try block on every preview. If `settings.json` is corrupt, partly written, or locked, `GetSettings` can throw `JsonException`, `IOException`, or `DirectoryNotFoundException`. The preview then fails with the internal-error path instead of just falling back to local images off.

I could not see what `SettingsUtils.GetSettings` throws, so this depends on that. Fix: catch `Exception` here and return `false`, or use `GetSettingsOrDefault`.
